label: chapter pages — the top bar follows the section, the corner menu holds its place, the hero lockup sits on the gutter
notes: Wil's four screenshots of 2026-09-18 (11:41-11:43 and 10:29), chapter pages only, three asks. (1) The area behind and around the minimized address bar is a solid fill in the colour of the section at the top of the viewport, updating with scroll; the bottom toolbar takes NO fill (his answer to question 1). Two mechanisms: <body> follows the section at the top edge (the round-21 rule, extended from /map to data-top-bar=section), and a new in-flow .edge-cover paints the same colour over whatever has scrolled past the top edge, which is what the minimized bar shows through its glass; round 18's hypothesis-2 strips, which his screenshots show did not take, are retired. Residue he was told about: Safari applies its one <body> tint to both bars. (2) The corner menu 'slides' on scroll: --ui-inset takes env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 0 to 34px as the bars collapse, so the burger moved 14px down and left with every retreat; the top-right menu now reads its own --menu-inset (gutter, top and right insets). The fade is kept (his answer to question 3). (3) The chapter hero's lockup inset becomes the gutter on phones, with the title's line-box slack taken out so the ink sits one gutter above the toolbar, and on tablets only in a browser with collapsing bars (his answer to question 4); the Part-2 hero and desktop are untouched. allowedRoutes is the five chapter routes because their 390 shots move by design (the lockup); 768 and 1440 must not drift, the menu's rest position is unchanged where insets are 0, and the cover is display:none in Chromium.
